headline: Carnegie's Higher Images Nominated for 2026 Best Places to Work
deck: After three straight first-place finishes, the Carnegie digital marketing agency is up again for a Pittsburgh Business Times workplace honor built on 25 years of local growth.
body:
On a quiet stretch of East Main Street in Carnegie, a marketing agency that has spent a quarter-century quietly building websites and ad campaigns for clients across the country just picked up another line on its resume. Higher Images, the full-service digital marketing and advertising firm headquartered in the borough, has been nominated for the 2026 Pittsburgh Business Times Best Places to Work program, following three consecutive years in which it took first place in its category.

For a company that started in 2000 as a small website shop, the streak says as much about staying power as it does about culture. Higher Images has since grown into an agency offering search engine optimization, paid advertising, social media management, branding, public relations and, increasingly, artificial intelligence services, serving businesses throughout the Pittsburgh region and beyond from its Carnegie headquarters and a satellite office on Pittsburgh's North Side.

Culture as a Growth Strategy

President Linda Jo Thornberg said the latest nomination reflects something harder to manufacture than a good ad campaign: a workplace where employees feel invested in the outcome. The Best Places to Work program, run by the Pittsburgh Business Times, leans heavily on employee feedback covering satisfaction, leadership and communication, meaning the honor is effectively a vote from the people doing the work.

"Technology can make a company faster, but people make it better. Our future depends on giving our team the tools, support and confidence to keep learning."

Linda Jo Thornberg, President, Higher Images

That philosophy has been tested repeatedly over the agency's history. Search engines change their algorithms, social platforms rise and fall, and now artificial intelligence is reshaping how businesses find customers online. Thornberg said keeping a team intact and motivated through those shifts has required treating employees as partners in figuring out what comes next, not just executors of a fixed playbook.

By The Numbers
25+Years in business, headquartered in Carnegie since 2000
10,000+Websites designed and developed for clients
10M+Leads generated through the agency's marketing campaigns
3Consecutive first-place Best Places to Work finishes before this year's nomination

The agency is also using the moment to point toward where it's headed next. Higher Images says it is expanding into AI search optimization, custom GPT development, AI-assisted reporting and chatbot design, betting that the same collaborative culture that won over Best Places to Work judges will help it navigate another technology shift the way it navigated the last several.

What It Means for Carnegie

Recognition programs like Best Places to Work rarely make headlines the way a nine-figure development deal does, but they matter for a different reason: they're a signal about which small and mid-sized Pittsburgh-area employers are quietly winning the talent competition that keeps a regional economy healthy. Carnegie, a borough of roughly 8,000 people a few miles southwest of Downtown, doesn't often get cast as a business hub. A homegrown company competing for a top regional workplace honor for a fourth straight cycle is a reminder that some of Pittsburgh's steadiest growth stories are happening a few blocks off Main Street, not just in the high-rises Downtown.

Winners of the 2026 Best Places to Work program are expected to be announced later this year. Whatever the outcome, Thornberg said the agency's approach won't change: keep investing in the people who show up every day, and let the workplace culture speak for itself in the results.
